key_insight: SCAPS-1D optimization suggests that an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 heterostructure can dramatically improve thin-film solar-cell performance, reaching a predicted 28.44% efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for absorber tuning, charge-selective layer engineering, and defect/recombination control in earth-abundant chalcogenide photovoltaics.
method: Modeled band alignment, electric fields, carrier distribution, and generation-recombination in SCAPS-1D.
Optimized absorber/transport-layer thicknesses, doping, defect densities, recombination, resistance, temperature, and light intensity.
Compared predicted performance against previously reported CNGS solar-cell efficiency ranges.
evidence_signal: The optimized device is reported to achieve 28.44% PCE with 0.984 V Voc, 34.39 mA/cm² Jsc, and 84.04% FF under AM1.5G illumination at 300 K.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions, so experimental verification is needed to confirm material quality, interface stability, and achievable defect levels.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
